Common_NoRowsHint: No rows yet - click + to add.
HelpDialog_LayerGroundDesc: Up to 5 layers drawn below players, NPCs, and items. Layer 1 is the base floor.
HelpDialog_LayerAnimFlagDesc: Tick the Anim box before painting to flag that layer as animated - it flashes on the animation tick. Works on any Ground, Fringe, or Canopy layer.
HelpDialog_LayerTilesetDesc: Each layer can use any loaded tileset; choose the sheet from the Tileset box (type a name or index). Sheets live in assets/graphics/tiles/ named with a leading index, e.g. 0_Tiles.bmp, 1_Cave.bmp - the number is the stable sheet index. Alt + scroll changes the active layer.
HelpDialog_LayerFringeDesc: Up to 5 layers drawn between the Ground- and Fringe-plane entity passes - the walkable surface of a bridge deck. Pair with a Layer Ramp attribute at each end so it can be mounted from Ground.
HelpDialog_LayerCanopyDesc: Up to 5 layers drawn above everything - players and NPCs on both planes (treetops, roofs, overhangs).
HelpDialog_LayersIntro: Each tile has three layer types - Ground (drawn below all entities), Fringe (the walkable bridge-deck surface, drawn between the Ground- and Fringe-plane entity passes), and Canopy (drawn above everything - treetops, roofs, overhangs) - each a stack of up to 5 layers composited bottom-to-top. Pick the layer type and number in the tools panel; right-click clears the hovered cell's selected layer, left-click fills it only if empty.
HelpDialog_SelectionIntro: Select mode lets you grab a rectangular region of the map and paste it elsewhere. The clipboard is mode-specific: a tile copy can only be pasted in Tile mode, an attribute copy only in Attribute mode. In Tile mode the source layer doesn't matter — paste always lands on the layer currently selected. Paste follows the same rule as regular placement: cells already occupied on the destination layer (or with a conflicting attribute) are skipped, and empty cells in the trimmed clipboard preserve the original gap structure.
HelpDialog_AttributesIntro: Attributes govern a tile's in-game behavior. In the two-plane world each attribute is authored on a logical layer - Ground (the base level) or Fringe (a bridge deck above it) - chosen with the Layer selector in the tools panel or Ctrl+Alt+scroll; the hover cursor shows G or F. Layer Ramp is the special connector between the planes. Right-click clears the active layer's attribute.
HelpDialog_Ctrl_LeftClickDesc: Paint tile or place attribute on hovered cell
HelpDialog_Ctrl_AltClickDesc: Place attribute with retained values, skipping the dialog (attribute mode only)
HelpDialog_Ctrl_CtrlDragDesc: Pan the map canvas by dragging
HelpDialog_Ctrl_CtrlAltShiftClickDesc: Switch to the surrounding map at the clicked cell — same as selecting it in the map list. If the clicked cell is a Warp tile on the active (center) map, jumps to the warp's destination map instead. No-op on an empty cell or on the active map with no warp under the cursor.
HelpDialog_Ctrl_RightClickDesc: Clear the active tile layer or remove attribute
HelpDialog_Ctrl_BackForwardDesc: Navigate back / forward through previously selected maps. Every map switch (list pick, neighbor click, or warp jump) is pushed onto the history stack.
HelpDialog_Ctrl_MouseBackForwardDesc: The side buttons on most modern mice — wired to the same Back / Forward navigation.
HelpDialog_Ctrl_ShiftHoldDesc: Show the exploded tile view — per-layer indices and attribute for the hovered cell (suppressed while Ctrl is held)
HelpDialog_Ctrl_AltScrollWheelDesc: Step the active layer index (number) up or down within the current layer type (clamped to 1-5).
HelpDialog_Ctrl_CtrlAltScrollWheelDesc: Change the active layer, clamped (no wrap). Tile mode cycles the layer type (Ground / Fringe / Canopy); Attribute & Light mode flips the logical plane (Ground / Fringe). The hover cursor shows the current layer - e.g. G4 / F1 in Tile mode, G / F in Attribute mode.
HelpDialog_Ctrl_SaveMapDesc: Write the selected map (or all dirty maps) to disk
HelpDialog_Ctrl_DiscardMapDesc: Reload the selected map (or all dirty maps) from disk, discarding unsaved changes
HelpDialog_Ctrl_PaletteClickDesc: Click a tile to use it as the brush; drag a rectangle on the tile palette to grab a multi-tile region as the brush.
HelpDialog_Sel_ActionPlaceDesc: Default action mode. Left-click stamps the selected tile (Tile mode) or attribute (Attribute mode). Drag continues stamping along the path.
HelpDialog_Sel_ActionSelectionDesc: Left-click and drag on the map to outline a rectangular selection (bright white). The selection lives only on the current map and clears if you switch maps.
HelpDialog_Sel_CtrlCSelectionDesc: Copy the selection to the clipboard. Tile mode copies only the currently selected layer; Attribute mode copies the attribute type and its data fields. The clipboard is automatically trimmed to the smallest rectangle containing real content, preserving internal gaps. The selection rectangle clears after copying. If nothing was copyable the existing clipboard is left untouched.
HelpDialog_Sel_CtrlCPlaceDesc: Brush-erases the active content (tile-art layer, attribute, or light — by mode) under an adjustable brush. Like right-click, but sized.
HelpDialog_Sel_CtrlXSelectionDesc: Cut — copies the selection then clears those cells (Tile mode clears the selected layer; Attribute mode clears the attribute). Undoable in one step.
HelpDialog_Sel_CtrlVSelectionDesc: Switch edit mode: Tile, Attribute, or Light (reads left to right).
HelpDialog_Sel_ClickPlaceDesc: Pastes the clipboard at the cursor. Clipboard is cleared after the paste.
HelpDialog_Sel_CtrlShiftClickDesc: Pastes the clipboard and retains it for re-pasting. The exploded tile view is suppressed while Ctrl is held, so the preview is unobstructed.
HelpDialog_Sel_EscDesc: Select mode: clears the selection rectangle. Place mode: clears the clipboard. With a Warp/Item Spawn/Key dialog open: closes the dialog.
HelpDialog_Attr_BlockedDesc: Hard wall. Neither players nor NPCs can enter this tile.
HelpDialog_Attr_WarpDesc: Teleports the player the moment they step on it. Set the destination map, X, and Y. The player arrives at exactly those coordinates.
HelpDialog_Attr_ItemDesc: Spawns a floor item that players can pick up. After collection it respawns after the configured delay. Respawn Seconds 0 uses the server default (120 s).
HelpDialog_Attr_ItemData: Data: Item · Value · Respawn Seconds (0 = 120 s default)
HelpDialog_Attr_NpcAvoidDesc: Passable for players, but NPCs will not path through it.
HelpDialog_Attr_KeyDesc: Blocks movement until a player possessing the required item interacts with the tile. Once unlocked, all players on the map can pass through. The door re-locks after 5 seconds. If 'Take key on use' is checked, the key item is consumed on unlock.
HelpDialog_Attr_KeyDoorDesc: Door reveal: paint the door's top graphic on the highest Ground layer, with a floor or base on the layers below it, then mark the tile Key. When the door is open only the topmost populated Ground layer is hidden (revealing what sits beneath); use the toolbar Doors toggle to preview the open state in the editor.
HelpDialog_Attr_KeyData: Data: Key Item · Take on use (0 = keep, 1 = consume)
HelpDialog_Attr_KeyOpenDesc: A trigger tile. Stepping on it automatically unlocks the Key tile at the specified coordinates — no item required.
HelpDialog_Attr_KeyOpenData: Data: Key Tile X · Key Tile Y (coordinates of the Key tile on this map)
HelpDialog_Attr_NpcSpawnDesc: Pins a map NPC slot to this tile so it always spawns here instead of a random walkable tile. Click an eligible (non-empty, unpinned) slot in the NPC Slots list to place it; right-click a pinned tile to clear it.
HelpDialog_Attr_LayerRampDesc: The connector between the two logical planes - the 'hole' between the Ground level and a Fringe bridge deck above it. A ramp is solid on the ground (you cannot walk under or through it) and walkable only on the Fringe surface, so the only way onto a bridge is up a ramp from its Ground-side foot. Place it on a fully clear tile (it cannot share a tile with any other attribute on either plane) and set the Ground-side direction. Occupies both planes; right-click removes it from either.
HelpDialog_Attr_LayerRampData: Data: Ground-side direction (the low end you mount from)

ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentDurability: • Durability: the starting durability assigned to the item when picked up or given. Weapons lose 1 per attack landed; armor/helmets lose 1 per hit received; shields lose 1 per magic hit and per block. At 5 remaining the player gets a warning; at 0 the item breaks and stays in the bag, unequipped, until repaired. 0 = no durability budget, so the piece never wears.
ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentPower: • Power (shown as Damage on a weapon, Defense on armor/helmet/shield): one number doing three jobs. It is the bonus granted while equipped (routed through diminishing-returns helpers — modest values keep nearly all their effect, extreme values soft-cap), it doubles as the minimum stat required to equip the item, and it sets the gold-per-point repair rate:
ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentWeapon: Weapon → bonus damage (2× GearMit shape, asymp 2×Str) & min STR to equip
ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentArmor: Armor  → bonus phys defense (GearMit DR, asymp Def) & min DEF to equip
ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentHelmet: Helmet → bonus phys defense (GearMit DR, asymp Def) & min DEF to equip
ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentShield: Shield → bonus defense (GearMit/4, paired with Def) & min DEF to equip
ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentClassReq: • Allowed Classes: restricts the item to the ticked classes. Leave every box unticked and anyone meeting the stat requirement can equip it. Tick one or more to gate the piece — useful for class-exclusive tiers where a tank class gets slightly more Power than a general piece, or for gear shared by a whole group such as all three Strength classes. Server enforces; the client tooltip lists the allowed classes.
ItemEditor_Notes_EquipmentShieldSide: • Shield side-effects: while equipped, run-stamina drains at 2 SP/tile (vs 1 normally). Mobility tradeoff for the magic-block + physical-block.
ItemEditor_Notes_PotionsAmount: • Amount = how much of the vital is added or subtracted when the potion is used. Add potions are clamped to the player’s maximum vital; Sub potions are clamped to 0 (cannot go negative) and restore half the amount on each of the other two vitals. The item is consumed on use.
ItemEditor_Notes_SpellScrollSpell: • Spell Number = the spell (1-based index) the scroll teaches. On use, the spell is added to the player’s spell list if they don’t already know it and have a free spell slot. The scroll is consumed on a successful learn.
ItemEditor_Notes_KeyId: • A key carries no fields of its own. Key-type tiles in the map editor name the item that opens them by ITEM NUMBER, so this item’s own slot number is its key id — different key items open different doors. Whether the key is consumed is set on the tile, not here.
ItemEditor_Notes_CurrencyDesc: • Stacks: picking up currency adds to an existing stack rather than filling a new inventory slot. No Data fields are used — the quantity is tracked by the inventory slot's value field.
NpcEditor_ExtraHpNote: Flat bonus max-HP, added 1:1 on top of the stat-derived pool (0 = none). Author bosses / walls or buff significant NPCs beyond what their combat stats imply -- HP is derived from total stat investment, so this is how you make something exceptionally tanky without inflating its other stats. Grants PREMIUM kill-EXP -- epic HP earns epic EXP, more per point than natural stat HP.
NpcEditor_LevelNote: The NPC's virtual level -- what level a player with this point spread would be (all four stats, SPD included: floor((statSum - 20) / 3) + 1). It drives HP/MP, mitigation, EXP, and the on-target strength readout alike. SPD buys durability (a higher level floor), never damage.
NpcEditor_Formula_VitalsMaxHp: Max HP   = baseHp × (100 + favorPct) / 100 × 1.5 + Extra HP
NpcEditor_Formula_VitalsNote: HP is DEF-driven off npcLevel (folded from total stat investment) so a balanced NPC matches an equivalent-level player -- there is no STR-to-HP bonus. Favor grows 0% to 20% across the stat range so endgame NPCs are slightly tankier. The × 1.5 pool multiplier lengthens fights, matching the player pools. Extra HP is a flat 1:1 designer add for bosses or HP buffs. MP mirrors HP off INT. SP is linear (Spd × 2, the player rate); NPCs run when chasing (and casters when kiting) and can sustain a run for a decent stretch -- the escape lever is SPEED, since an NPC run caps just below the player's.
NpcEditor_Formula_RegenHeader: NPC Regen (per 5s tick — HP paused in combat)
NpcEditor_Formula_RegenNote: HP and MP regen match the pool shape (including the × 1.5 pool multiplier) so regen-as-%-of-pool stays roughly constant. NPC tick is 5 s flat, about half the per-second rate of the player's 2.5 s OOC cadence. NPC HP regen is suppressed during combat (mirrors player HP); NPC MP/SP regen runs every tick regardless.
NpcEditor_Formula_CombatMDmg: M-DMG = SpellPower(INT) + SpellContribution(INT, INT)   (mirror of P-DMG, off INT)
NpcEditor_Formula_CombatMit: MIT = NpcProtection(DEF) = PlayerProtection(DEF) + 2 x GearMitigation(DEF, DEF)   (one axis: resists P-DMG and M-DMG alike)
NpcEditor_Formula_CombatFloor: Damage taken = max(raw - MIT, raw x floor). The floor means mitigation is never immunity: 12% for an ordinary NPC, 19% when Boss is ticked. It only binds once MIT has eaten ~81% of the raw -- in practice only a dedicated tank, whose mitigation outgrows NPC damage at every level. Against anyone else subtraction wins and the Boss flag changes nothing about damage dealt.
NpcEditor_Formula_CombatNote: NPCs use the exact same combat helpers as players, at matched implicit gear (Power = stat). STR and INT are mirror offense stats and DEF is the single defense axis, so P-DMG and M-DMG share one curve and one MIT resists both. No damage or mit favor -- HP-only favor handles the ‘NPC slightly stronger’ feel. Each hit rolls a symmetric +/-10% (the same Vary as melee). MP cost scales with the cast magnitude, and a caster’s MP pool is sized to outlast a full fight against an equal-level foe.
NpcEditor_Formula_ExpLine1: EXP = max((STR + DEF + INT) × 30 + baseHp + Extra HP × 2, 1)
NpcEditor_Formula_ExpLine2: baseHp is the DEF-driven HP pool (pre-favor, pre-× 1.5); Extra HP earns a 2× EXP premium
NpcEditor_Formula_ExpNote: Stat sum × 30 pays for each stat's non-HP roles (offense, mitigation, block/dodge/regen). The baseHp term rewards fight-length -- a tankier NPC is worth proportionally more -- and is skipped for a fully statless filler NPC. Extra HP earns a 2× premium (epic HP means epic EXP for a boss slog). SPD is excluded: it only gates %-bounded events and movement.
NpcEditor_Formula_DropChanceLine1: chance = Drop Chance %   (the number is the drop percentage)
NpcEditor_Formula_DropChanceNote: Drop Chance is a direct percentage from 0 to 100. Higher values drop more often, and anything above 100 is capped at 100%. The Drop % preview above shows the resulting chance.
NpcEditor_Formula_ChancesNote: All three require SP > 0 at the moment of the check. A crit costs 10% max SP; a block costs 10% max SP; a dodge costs 20% max SP. Each hit randomly selects either block or dodge to attempt (50/50) — only the chosen one is rolled, then crit is checked if neither triggered. Spell crit mirrors melee crit but rolls off INT instead of STR (same 25% cap).
SpellEditor_MpCostNote: (SubHp: trivial pool MP + the reagent below. AddMp is priced off what it restores, so its cost rises with the caster's INT — the figure shown is for the weakest caster who could learn it. Other types show their fixed utility MP cost.)

ClassEditor_Formula_VitalsNote: HP and MP use a shifted-quadratic shape so pools grow noticeably with level. SP stays linear because SP costs are %-of-pool, so a quadratic SP pool would just inflate event counts without changing fight feel. Each class stat maps to a vital: classDEF → HP, classINT → MP, classSPD → SP. classSTR adds only a marginal HP top-up (≤ +20%); classDEF also drives HP regen and physical mitigation.
ClassEditor_Formula_RegenHeader: Regen (per tick, uses player's own stats)
ClassEditor_Formula_RegenSp: SP regen = max(playerSPD / 2, 2)               ← linear (matches linear SP pool)
ClassEditor_Formula_RegenNote: HP and MP regen match the pool shape so regen-as-%-of-pool stays roughly constant (~7-10%) at every level. Cadences: HP ticks every 2.5 s out of combat (1.25 s in safe zone), paused in combat; MP/SP tick every 2.5 s out of combat (1 s in safe zone), 10 s in combat.
ClassEditor_Formula_CombatNote: Weapons add to P-DMG and a prepared spell adds to M-DMG through the SAME diminishing-returns curve -- a spell is a weapon delivered at range. Armor/helmet stack onto MIT; a shield adds to MIT at 1/4 the gear rate. One MIT resists physical and magic identically. The preview values above show only what the class itself brings -- the bare-handed floor.
ClassEditor_Formula_PreviewNote: Preview values shown above assume Level=1 and playerStat = classStat (the one-time stat copy at character creation). After creation a player allocates 3 stat points per level into whichever stats they choose, so live numbers diverge from this preview as they progress.
SpellEditor_Formula_MagnitudeIntro: Amount is the spell’s magnitude — and it controls three things at once:
SpellEditor_Formula_MagnitudeBullet1: • Primary effect (heal amount, damage or drain magnitude) — passed through diminishing returns, so the spell’s own contribution asymptotes at 2 × INT however large the number gets
SpellEditor_Formula_MagnitudeBullet2: • Base level requirement: max(1, Amount − classINT/4) — raw, not DR’d, so high-magnitude spells stay level-gated
SpellEditor_Formula_MagnitudeBullet3: • Cost — utility spells (Add*, SubMp, SubSp) pay max(1, (Amount + 15)^1.5 / 6) MP; SubHp instead pays a trivial MaxMP / 20 plus round(Amount / 10 × ~0.48) reagents per cast. Either way the cost comes off the RAW Amount while the damage is diminished, so past a point more Amount buys cost without buying damage — that is the ceiling, not a bug.
SpellEditor_Formula_ClassIntNote: classINT (the class's base INT) reduces both the level requirement and the MP cost at the same time — one number doing two jobs.
SpellEditor_Formula_PlayerIntNote: playerINT (stat points the player has personally allocated) has no effect on cost or level gating. It drives spell magnitude via SpellPower and SpellContribution -- the exact mirror of how STR drives melee. INT provides no defense; DEF is the single defense axis for physical and magic alike.
SpellEditor_Formula_MagnitudeRaw: raw       = max((playerINT + 20)^1.5 / 10, 1)         <- SpellPower(INT), = UnarmedDamage off INT
SpellEditor_Formula_MagnitudeContributio: + 2 x Amount x INT / (INT + Amount)        <- SpellContribution (mirrors a weapon; asymp 2xINT)
SpellEditor_Formula_MagnitudeActualHit: actualHit = raw - targetMIT                            (x2 on spell crit; dodgeable + shield-blockable)
SpellEditor_Formula_MagnitudeMitNote: Target MIT = (DEF + 20)^1.5 / 20 -- the single universal mitigation, identical to physical (the mirror deleted the separate magic resist and its penetration). Players add gear MIT from each defensive piece (armor/helmet full, shield 1/4); a spell can be DODGED, and an equipped shield can BLOCK it outright at the same SP as a melee block. NPCs add 2 implicit matched gear pieces. Heals scale through the same magnitude formula; the result is added to HP/MP/SP instead of subtracted, with no MIT applied.
SpellEditor_Formula_MpCostFormula: Utility (AddHp / AddSp / SubMp / SubSp): max(1, (Amount + 15)^1.5 / 6), ×1.10 for AddSp (AddHp untaxed).  AddMp: ceil(restore × 1.30), where restore = SpellPower(casterINT) + contribution(Amount, casterINT).  SubHp: MP = MaxMP / 20 (trivial); cost = round(Amount / 10 × ~0.48) reagents per cast.
SpellEditor_Formula_MpCostNote: SubHp is the caster’s sustainable ‘weapon’: its MP is a trivial fraction of the pool (mana funds utility — heals and drains — not basic damage), and its real per-cast cost is the reagent, the magic mirror of weapon-repair upkeep — round(Amount / 10 × ~0.48), where a spell’s Amount mirrors a weapon’s Power, /10 is the repair gold per durability, and ~0.48 is the average durability a swing actually chips. Utility spells pay the metadata MP cost. AddMp is the other exception, and for the opposite reason: mana is the vital it restores AND the vital it spends, so pricing it off the authored Amount alone let a self-cast net positive — the restore carries a SpellPower(casterINT) term that an Amount-only cost has no term for. It is therefore priced off what it actually hands over, ×1.30, which keeps it a loss on yourself at every INT and makes it a transfer to allies at roughly 77% efficiency. The 30% (rather than bare parity) covers spell crits, which inflate the expected restore to about 1.18× at the 35% crit cap.
SpellEditor_Formula_GiveItemBullet1: • GiveItem has no Amount at all. Item Number is a pure identifier and does NOT contribute to MP cost or level requirement.
SpellEditor_Formula_GiveItemBullet2: • Quantity is how many, written to Inv.Value on grant. Only Currency items use this; non-currency items always come as one per cast.
SpellEditor_Formula_GiveItemBullet3: • INT Requirement is what GiveItem gates and prices off instead: level req = max(1, INTReq − classINT/4); MP cost = max(1, (INTReq + 15)^1.5 / 6).
SpellEditor_Formula_MaxMpNote: Shifted-quadratic — pools grow noticeably with level. At Level 1 with a fresh-creation playerINT = classINT, Max MP = (1 + 1.5 × classINT + 15)² / 15. Use these bounds when designing Max MP Cost values.
SpellEditor_Formula_RangeNote: 81 castable tiles total. Range is symmetric by construction, so PvP exchanges are two-way.
